concepts.title: Meaning and Scope of Social Science

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Scope of Social Science' refers to.
questions.a: Social science is the study of human society and social relationships, covering how people live, organise themselves, and interact with one another and their environment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Scope of Social Science'.
questions.a: Social science explores human society, behaviour, and relationships across time and space.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Meaning and Scope of Social Science'.
questions.a: What is social science?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Branches of Social Science: History' refers to.
questions.a: History is the study of past events, societies, and civilisations, based on written records and archaeological evidence, to understand how human societies have changed over time.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Branches of Social Science: History'.
questions.a: History helps us understand the present by studying the past events and societies that shaped it.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Branches of Social Science: History'.
questions.a: What is history as a branch of social science?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Branches of Social Science: Geography' refers to.
questions.a: Geography is the study of the Earth's surface, its physical features, climate, and the relationship between humans and their environment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Branches of Social Science: Geography'.
questions.a: Geography links natural features of the Earth with how humans use and adapt to their environment.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Branches of Social Science: Geography'.
questions.a: What is geography as a branch of social science?

concepts.title: Branches of Social Science: Political Science

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Branches of Social Science: Political Science' refers to.
questions.a: Political science is the study of government, political processes, and institutions, and how power and authority are organised and used in society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Branches of Social Science: Political Science'.
questions.a: Political science studies how governments work and how power is organised and used in society.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Branches of Social Science: Political Science'.
questions.a: What is political science?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Branches of Social Science: Economics' refers to.
questions.a: Economics is the study of how people, businesses, and governments produce, distribute, and consume goods and services to satisfy human wants.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Branches of Social Science: Economics'.
questions.a: Economics studies how resources are used to produce and distribute goods and services to meet human needs.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Branches of Social Science: Economics'.
questions.a: What is economics as a branch of social science?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Relevance of Social Science' refers to.
questions.a: Social science is relevant because it helps us understand society, solve social problems, make informed decisions, and become responsible citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Relevance of Social Science'.
questions.a: Social science is relevant because it builds awareness of society and helps citizens make informed decisions.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Relevance of Social Science'.
questions.a: Why is social science relevant today?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Indian Perspective on Social Science' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian perspective on social science draws on India's diverse cultures, traditions, and historical experiences to understand society, emphasising unity in diversity and the country's plural heritage.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Indian Perspective on Social Science'.
questions.a: The Indian perspective views social science through the lens of India's diversity, plural heritage, and unity in diversity.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Indian Perspective on Social Science'.
questions.a: What is the Indian perspective on social science?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Interconnections Between Disciplines' refers to.
questions.a: The branches of social science are interconnected because history, geography, political science, and economics all influence one another and together explain human society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Interconnections Between Disciplines'.
questions.a: The branches of social science are linked; events and processes studied in one branch often affect the others.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Interconnections Between Disciplines'.
questions.a: How are the branches of social science interconnected?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Methods of Social Science' refers to.
questions.a: Methods of social science are the ways social scientists study society, including observation, surveys, interviews, case studies, and analysis of sources and data.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Methods of Social Science'.
questions.a: Social scientists use methods like observation, surveys, and source analysis to study society systematically.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Methods of Social Science'.
questions.a: What are the methods of social science?

concepts.title: Sources and Evidence in Social Science

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources and Evidence in Social Science' refers to.
questions.a: Sources and evidence in social science are the materials and records, such as documents, artefacts, oral traditions, and data, that scholars use to build and support their understanding of society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources and Evidence in Social Science'.
questions.a: Social science relies on sources and evidence, both primary and secondary, to build reliable knowledge about society.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Sources and Evidence in Social Science'.
questions.a: What are sources in social science?
